prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1028; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a report of a low-speed head-on collision in Pearland, Texas. Driver 1 was traveling in the northbound lane when the front of their vehicle made contact with the front of a vehicle operated by Driver 2, which was southbound. Both drivers stayed at the scene and cooperated with the investigation. Driver 1 reported neck strain and was evaluated by responding medical personnel. The reported injury is consistent with the type and force of this impact. Driver 2 confirmed the sequence of events as Driver 1 described it. Two independent witnesses gave statements that matched the account, and scene photographs show damage to the front ends of both vehicles that corresponds to the reported impact. Officers found no indication of prior damage to either vehicle. Driver 1 is listed as a named insured on the policy covering the vehicle. Officers were unable to confirm the seating position of the Passenger at the moment of impact, as the Passenger's account varied between statements. No citations were issued at the scene.
